bib.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

question: Can a straightforward encoder-decoder application of deep LSTMs learn general sequence-to-sequence mapping, tested on English to French machine translation?
hypothesis: An LSTM encoding the source into a fixed vector and a second LSTM decoding it can handle sequences with minimal structural assumptions, and reversing source word order shortens time lags and eases optimisation.
contributions: A deep LSTM encoder-decoder that directly translates and beats a phrase-based SMT baseline on WMT'14 En-Fr
Reversing source sentences (not targets) as a key technical trick
Sentence representations sensitive to word order and fairly invariant to active/passive voice

method.summary: Two 4-layer LSTMs (encoder reads the reversed source into a fixed vector, decoder is a conditional LSTM language model) trained with SGD on 12M WMT'14 En-Fr sentence pairs; decoding by left-to-right beam search, plus rescoring of the baseline SMT 1000-best lists. Ensembles of 5 models differ in random initialisation and minibatch order.
method.task: English to French machine translation (sequence to sequence)

datasets.name: WMT'14 English to French (selected subset)
datasets.size: 12M sentences, 348M French words and 304M English words
datasets.split: ntst14 test set used for evaluation; no dev set or split sizes stated
datasets.source: clean 'selected' subset from Schwenk-style baseline reference [29]; tokenized train/test and baseline SMT 1000-best lists publicly available
datasets.preprocessing: Fixed vocabularies: 160,000 most frequent source words and 80,000 most frequent target words; out-of-vocabulary words replaced by 'UNK'; each sentence ends with <EOS>; source sentences reversed

datasets.name: WMT'14 En-Fr ntst14 test set and baseline SMT 1000-best lists

models.name: Deep LSTM encoder-decoder (single)
models.architecture: two separate LSTMs (encoder, decoder), LSTM formulation from Graves; naive softmax over 80,000 words
models.hidden: 1000 cells per layer; 1000-dim word embeddings; 8000 real numbers represent a sentence

models.name: Ensemble of 5 deep LSTMs
models.architecture: same as single model, differing in random initialisation and minibatch order

training.objective: maximise average log probability of correct translation T given source S: 1/|S| sum over (T,S) of log p(T|S)
training.lr_schedule: after 5 epochs, halve the learning rate every half epoch
training.batch_size: 128 sequences (gradient divided by 128); sentences in a minibatch of roughly equal length (2x speedup)
training.regularisation: hard gradient norm clipping: s = ||g||2 with g divided by 128; if s > 5, g = 5g/s
training.hardware: 8-GPU machine: one GPU per LSTM layer (4), other 4 GPUs parallelise the softmax (each multiplies by a 1000 x 20000 matrix)
training.compute: C++ implementation; 1,700 words/s on a single GPU, 6,300 words/s (English and French) on 8 GPUs at minibatch 128
training.seeds: ensemble of 5 models differing in random initialisation and minibatch order

other.deep_vs_shallow: each additional layer reduced perplexity by nearly 10%

inference.decoding: simple left-to-right beam search; B partial hypotheses; hypotheses completed when <EOS> appended; rescoring: even average of baseline score and LSTM log probability over SMT 1000-best
inference.samples: ensemble of 5 models; Table 1 beam sizes 1, 2, 12

parameters.rescoring_weights: even average of the two scores

metrics.name: cased BLEU
metrics.definition: multi-bleu.pl on tokenized predictions and ground truth; consistent with Cho et al. and Bahdanau et al.; reproduces 33.3 of [29]

limits: Fixed vocabulary of 80k target words; BLEU penalised on OOV (UNK) and the model cannot handle out-of-vocabulary words (Sec 3.6; Table 3 shows UNK emitted for a name).
Authors have no complete explanation for why reversal works; the short-term-dependency account is a belief (Sec 3.3).
Authors believe a standard RNN would be trainable on reversed sources but did not verify it (Sec 5).
Pure LSTM ensemble does not beat the best WMT'14 system (37.0).
Fixed-size 8000-dim sentence vector bottleneck; attention (Bahdanau 2014) is cited as the alternative that addressed long-sentence weakness.
Single test set and no variance or significance reporting; no code or weights released in the paper.
Sec 3.5: the 2x speedup from equal-length batching and training times are for 2014 hardware.

terms.definition: The smallest distance between a source word and its corresponding target word in the concatenated sequence; reversal greatly reduces it while average distance is unchanged.
